package.name: P2D2
package.description:
COMPSCI Robotics – Project 2 Deliverable 2
This package implements reinforcement learning for right-side wall following with the Triton robot in Gazebo using ROS Noetic. It supports both Q-learning and SARSA, and provides separate training and testing modes. Demonstration video links are provided at the bottom of the description section.
The controller uses LiDAR-based discrete states derived from:
Front-Right distance bin Front obstacle flag Front-Left distance bin
The action set consists of three discrete motion primitives:
FWD LEFT RIGHT
The Q-table is initialized from the manually defined Deliverable 1 policy and is updated during learning using temporal-difference reinforcement learning. Rewards are defined from task outcomes rather than directly rewarding specific actions. In other words, reward is purely state-based.
During training, the robot is reset each episode to one of several fixed pose-orientation pairs chosen at random so that it starts parallel to a wall on its right side. The package saves learned Q-tables in the data/ directory, best learned Q-table checkpoints, and per-episode accumulated reward logs for plotting and analysis.
In testing mode, the package loads the best learned Q-table and executes the learned greedy policy for evaluation in Gazebo.
This package requires the stingray_sim package, which provides the Triton robot model, the Gazebo world file used for training and testing, and the simulation launch infrastructure. Consequently, ensure the workspace contains both:
catkin_ws/src/stingray_sim catkin_ws/src/P2D2
Commands to run the demonstration:
cd ~/catkin_ws catkin_make source devel/setup.bash
Train Q-learning: roslaunch P2D2 p2d2.launch algorithm:=q_learning mode:=train
Test Q-learning: roslaunch P2D2 p2d2.launch algorithm:=q_learning mode:=test
Train SARSA: roslaunch P2D2 p2d2.launch algorithm:=sarsa mode:=train
Test SARSA: roslaunch P2D2 p2d2.launch algorithm:=sarsa mode:=test
Video Links:
Q-learning training: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1j2r_whLoWZ1LX6LLoJXSZ33P2LgDQlsz/view?usp=sharing
Q-learning testing: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1M8qKAGskxVRt2Ardk9v9eTbJ4B9fUhc9/view?usp=sharing
Sarsa training: https://drive.google.com/file/d/15N21yI22PMYfSndlublNo9xG2SFqFAVn/view?usp=sharing
Sarsa testing: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Zaf89cbymMf5McTDT5cLWC2dznxvKZI6/view?usp=sharing
During testing, if the robot spawns at the i-beam first, just restart the sim until it spawns somewhere else. Then, to show i-beam capabilities, run the following command during the test:
rosservice call /gazebo/set_model_state " > model_state: > model_name: 'triton' > pose: > position: > x: -1.1240135431289673 > y: -2.623599052429199 > z: 0.0 > orientation: > x: 8.453633199678734e-06 > y: -6.342688720906153e-06 > z: -0.7060427665710449 > w: -0.708169162273407 > twist: > linear: {x: 0.0, y: 0.0, z: 0.0} > angular: {x: 0.0, y: 0.0, z: 0.0} > reference_frame: 'world' > "
